summary:
Ondo is a state in south-western Nigeria and stands under Nigeria's national framework. The Same-Sex Marriage (Prohibition) Act 2014 and the secular criminal provisions covering same-sex conduct extend to Ondo in full. The sources record no Ondo statute, protective measure or enforcement divergence of the state's own, and Wikipedia's overview of LGBT rights in Nigeria does not name Ondo at all.

The Shari'a penalty layer does not reach Ondo. The twelve northern states operating Shari'a-based criminal codes, where male sodomy can carry death by stoning, are separate jurisdictions; as a southern state Ondo stands under the secular framework, where the maximum penalty recorded is a life sentence.

Same-sex sexual activity has been illegal across the country since 1916. The Same-Sex Marriage (Prohibition) Act was passed by the House of Representatives on 30 May 2013 and signed into law by President Goodluck Jonathan in January 2014, criminalising all forms of same-sex unions with up to 14 years' imprisonment.

The UK Home Office country policy and information note of June 2025 quotes Section 217 of the Criminal Code, under which any male who commits or procures an act of gross indecency with another male, in public or in private, is guilty of a felony liable to three years' imprisonment. That offence applies in southern states such as Ondo. Victor Oluwasina Ayeni, senior lecturer in law at Adekunle Ajasin University in Ondo state, observed in a January 2017 book chapter that the Code fails to define what constitutes an act of gross indecency.

The same Home Office note documents the national criminal framework applying across all states, including the 2014 statute, and records countrywide harm patterns of arrests, detention and mob violence against LGBT+ people. It confirms that the twelve northern states' Shari'a penal codes, with penalties up to death by stoning, remain in force, so that penalty layer does not extend to Ondo.

Wikipedia records no legal recognition of gender identity, no anti-discrimination protections and no recognition of same-sex relationships anywhere in the country, and Ondo supplies none of these itself.
tangentialFactors:
A visitor in Ondo faces two distinct criminal layers rather than one: the 14-year exposure under the 2014 act for same-sex unions and conduct, and the three-year felony exposure under Section 217 of the Criminal Code for gross indecency between males, public or private. The second offence carries a shorter term but a broader and undefined description of the prohibited act.

The death-penalty exposure reported for Nigeria applies only in the twelve northern states under Shari'a-based codes. A traveller comparing Nigerian destinations should treat Ondo and the northern states as separate penalty regimes, with the northern regime materially harsher.

The arrests, detention and mob violence recorded by the UK Home Office for June 2025 are documented countrywide without a state-by-state breakdown, so Ondo's share of that pattern cannot be separated out from the sources held here.
localsOnly:
Residents of Ondo have no state-level protection against discrimination on grounds of gender identity or sexual orientation, no legal recognition of gender identity, and no recognition of same-sex relationships. No state complaint mechanism, equality body or protective statute is documented.

The undefined scope of Section 217 of the Criminal Code leaves the description of a gross indecency offence to be settled case by case, a point made in a January 2017 book chapter by Victor Oluwasina Ayeni, a senior lecturer in law at Adekunle Ajasin University in Ondo state. For residents, that open definition shapes how the three-year felony provision is applied by prosecutors and courts in the state.

Enforcement practice by Ondo police, and any Ondo court decisions under either the 2014 act or Section 217, are not documented in the sources held here.
outOfScopeNotes:
No Ondo-specific arrest, prosecution, court decision, police action or incident of violence against a trans or gender-nonconforming person appears in the source inventory. The one documented killing of a transgender woman in the inventory, of the 33-year-old TikToker known as Abuja Area Mama, found beaten dead on 9 August 2024, occurred in Abuja and not in Ondo; police opened a 'thorough and discreet' investigation and the account records no charge. Whether comparable incidents have occurred in Ondo is unresolved and not sourced.

Whether Ondo police enforce the national framework more or less aggressively than other southern states is not sourced. The absence of Ondo's name from Wikipedia's overview of LGBT rights in Nigeria is an absence of coverage, not evidence of non-enforcement or of safety.

No Ondo-specific survey, arrest tally or violence statistic is available in the inventory, so no prevalence figure for the state can be stated.
